# SPILLWAY 1.0.1

> Prompt-injection defense for tool-using LLM agents: structure decides where an agent acts, an optional judge checks selected calls. SPILLWAY checks the recipients, accounts and channels of side-effecting tool calls against the user's task and the typed identity fields that read-only tools returned. Fixed delegation rules admit some targets the user named indirectly. A rule-based sanitizer removes instruction-like text before the model reads it. A local 4-bit judge (gemma4:31b), enabled with identity-target recovery in the displayed full-system results and off by default in the package, checks selected calls, including refused-target recovery and object checks. Two-view recovery does not restore a target that lies in removed text.

- Install: `pip install spillway-guard==1.0.1` (Python 3.10+, pydantic and PyYAML). Import name: `spillway_guard`.
- Current SDK: [1.0.1 release](https://github.com/saintmachines/spillway/releases/tag/v1.0.1), with reviewed boundary fixes. [SDK and mini host-variant scope](release-1.0.1-scope.md). The charts and tables below retain their historical measurements.
- Runtime provenance: 1.0.0 preserves the runtime measured in 0.1.4, with release metadata changes and unchanged experimental records. [Runtime equivalence](release-1.0.0.html#runtime-equivalence).
- App integration: [integrate.html](integrate.html), with a runnable local example in [examples/](examples/README.md)
- Paper: [arXiv:2611.07222](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.07222), [PDF](SPILLWAY_preprint.pdf)
- Code: https://github.com/saintmachines/spillway
- Results as JSON: [results.json](results.json). Full tables: [results.html](results.html)
- Authors: Woosang Lim (SAINT Machines and KAIST), Yeseul Chang and Jaewoo Lee (Chung-Ang University). Project of SAINT Machines: https://saintmachines.ai. Contact: contact@saintmachines.ai

## Headline results (AgentDojo v1.2.2, 3 backbones x 4 suites, in-scope attack success)
- SPILLWAY: 0 of 12 cells leak, utility under attack .489, benign utility .539 (undefended .540). These are SPILLWAY 1.0.0 results; comparison methods retain the paper results. Mini's four-suite scatter point is .608 utility and .000 ASR, separately from the twelve-cell .489 mean.
- MELON, Progent, DRIFT leak on 10, 11 and 7 of 12 cells. In the historical paper cost study on benign qwen3:8b Workspace and Slack episodes they add 3.25 to 9.91 model calls per episode. SPILLWAY adds 0.19 to 0.39, judge included.
- Seven-suite comparison: four current SPILLWAY AgentDojo rows (Banking .444, Slack .562, Travel .579, Workspace .848) combine with three historical AgentDyn rows (.600, .435, .383), all with .000 ASR. The mixed seven-suite utility mean is .550. All ROPE measurements are historical: its authors' Claude Opus 4.8 router has mean utility .468 and leaks on three suites. AgentDyn was not rerun.
- SPILLWAY 1.0.0 stress tests: ChatInject 0/665 effects, AutoDojo 0/389 (descriptive), sender 0/126. PISmith ASR@1 retains mini 4/949 effects (macro ASR .005, utility .257) and qwen3:8b 1/949 (macro ASR .002, utility .173). Historical held-out and latency studies remain paper measurements.

## Scope
The structural identity-target property depends on reviewed typed roles and transport contracts. It does not authenticate an attacker-written identity field or guarantee all content-only effects. Reported attack success retains each original family scorer's convention, including the recorded qwen PISmith calendar-integrity effect. See the artifact-bound report for denominators, context overflows and execution amendments.
